content.text:
View A: Four remembered items — upper is a green circle, right a red triangle, lower a blue square, left a yellow cross. Attention is currently on the left (the yellow cross); the other three are barely selected now. Recoverability estimates indicate the lower blue square is the most accessible over the next two steps, the left cross and upper green circle are moderately accessible, and the right red triangle is least accessible. Predicted effects of issuing different commands are similar: nearly every command drives predicted selection toward the upper location, with only tiny shifts to other locations. Thus the model shows little controllability of view A — alternative commands do not substantially change the predicted allocation.

View B: Four remembered items — upper a green triangle, right a red circle, lower a blue square, left a yellow cross. Attention is currently on the left (the yellow cross); right and upper have low but nonzero selection likelihoods and the lower square is the least currently attended. Recoverability patterns place the right and upper items as more recoverable than the lower item. Predicted command outcomes are strongly command-specific: commanding a location predicts selecting that same location. Therefore view B appears under good control: redirecting attention to a specific location is predicted to move allocation to that location.
